McLaren: McLaren has slapped on a brand‑new rear wing that gives the car a more stable, powerful push down the straights, helping it stick to the tarmac at top speed. At the same time they’ve reshaped the central engine cover and refined the rear brake ducts to smooth the airflow, which translates into extra grip in the corners and better cooling when the laps heat up. Together, these tweaks should make the car quicker through the twisty sections and more confident on the long straights for this weekend’s race.
Mercedes F1 Team: Mercedes has removed the drum‑shaped lip that was stuck on the front‑corner inlet and tweaked the camber angle, giving the front wheels cleaner airflow and a more balanced feel. The result should be a steadier front end, better cornering grip and less turbulence for the rest of the car – exactly what the team needs to stay competitive on this weekend’s track.
Red Bull Racing: Red Bull has tweaked the front‑corner aero pieces – they’ve shortened the wishbone shroud and reshaped the wheel‑rim cover – to boost reliability and keep the front end more stable under load. The changes should reduce the risk of a sudden suspension or wheel‑body failure and give the car a cleaner airflow package, meaning the team can push harder without worrying about a fragile front‑corner this weekend.
Scuderia Ferrari: Ferrari has re‑shaped the entire front‑floor package – tweaking the brace layout, the edge curl and the little vanes that sit under the car – to tighten up airflow and give a more consistent grip out of the corners. The diffuser has been given a new expansion profile and a revised fence, which should boost rear stability without adding drag, while the lower beam wing now carries a subtle twist that smooths the airflow along the car’s side. In short, the changes are aimed at delivering a steadier, more predictable downforce package, helping the drivers push harder through the high‑speed sections of this weekend’s circuit.
